slides.title: Alkylation-site question
bullets: The route question was where the alkyl group would be installed.
Desired substitution was favoured in the selected sequence.
Keep site assignment separate from the appearance of a clean chromatogram.
bullets_right: The delivered structures are isolated compounds.
The impurity reference supports recognition of the competing material.
No site-selectivity ratio is quoted in this readout.
Do not turn the route observation into a protease-inhibition claim.

slides.title: Impurity reference travels with the set
bullets: Retain the reference identity with the delivery paperwork.
Use the reference when comparing subsequent alkylation preparations.
The reference is supporting material, not a desired analogue.
Acceptance of the set does not remove the need to recognise the competing product.
slides.notes: My reminder: do not leave the impurity reference behind when splitting the analogue set for dispatch. Check the compound-card link first. — C. Antoine

slides.title: Handover before archiving
bullets: Christiane Antoine: working route notes and analogue context.
Hassan Darwish: follow-on synthetic route questions.
Clara Fenwick: released material and reference linkage.
bullets_right: Preserve the distinction between desired-site product and impurity reference.
Use mg from the delivery register for allocation; do not assume equal stock.

slides.title: Next analogue: retain the successful site preference
bullets: Use the accepted alkylation sequence as the initial route scout.
Check site assignment again when the substituent changes.
Keep the impurity reference available for comparison.
Close VD-20-028 with the accepted delivery; future structures remain proposals.
slides.notes: C. Antoine: final delivery copy, 10 Aug 2020. Leave the chemistry notes with this file so the route can be picked up without reconstructing the laptop folders.
